thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Tumble Weighs On Stocks; Dow On Track For 4th Straight Drop

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Tumble Weighs On Stocks; Dow On Track For 4th Straight Drop
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Tech sector poised for biggest one-day drop since July
U.S. stocks fell on Wednesday, with technology stocks leading the decline as they tumbled in their biggest one-day drop in months, providing an outsize drop to the Nasdaq.
Losses accelerated throughout the session as major tech firms, including Microsoft and Apple, extended their declines, putting the Dow on track for its fourth straight daily drop.
How are equity benchmarks performing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 43 points to 25,909, a decline of 0.2%. The S&P 500 lost 14 points, or 0.5%, to 2,882. The Nasdaq Composite Index sank 108 points to 7,983, a drop of 1.3%.
The Dow is on track to record its fourth straight decline, a losing streak it hasn't registered since mid-August, according to FactSet data.
Tech shares were the weakest of the day, with the sector down 1.6%, on track for the biggest one-day drop since July. That weighed on the Nasdaq, which has an outsize exposure to the industry. Among notable movers, Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell 1.2% and Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) was down 1.7%. Twitter Inc. (TWTR) sank 5.2% and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) lost 2.4%.
Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) fell 2.2%. While the e-commerce giant is classified as a consumer-discretionary company, it often trades on technology-related trends. Netflix Inc. (NFLX) fell 5%.
What's driving the market?
There was no clear catalyst for the drop in technology stocks, but the industry has been the top-performing sector of the year by far, beneficiaries of a long-term uptrend in momentum stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-stock-markets-best-investment-strategy-shows-no-sign-of-slowing-2018-09-05).
"I don't see any specific catalyst pushing tech lower, and it's pretty quiet from the perspective of news about these stocks, which makes me think this is a classic sector rotation," said Douglas DePietro, managing director for trading at Evercore ISI.
"These groups have been outperforming, and this could be an example of investors taking profits, particularly since September is a historically turbulent month and a lot of big banks and brokerage houses have been encouraging their clients to lighten up on their tech exposure."
Social-media companies were in focus as their executives -- including representatives from both Facebook and Twitter -- testified on Capital Hill about misinformation (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-must-work-together-to-win-misinformation-arms-race-facebook-ceo-says-2018-09-04). DePietro said that while traders were watching the testimony, nothing market-moving had yet come out of the event.
Trade policy also remained in focus, with the U.S. and Canada set to restart high-stakes efforts to resolve trade differences as they work toward recasting the North American Free Trade Agreement. Discussions have been tense at times with President Donald Trump over the Labor Day weekend threatening to move forward without the northern neighbor (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/new-nafta-is-doomed-unless-it-includes-canada-union-leader-says-2018-09-02) if it can't agree to terms. On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau reiterated the country's view that "no Nafta is better than a bad Nafta deal for Canadians, and that's what we are going to stay with."
Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland is set to meet U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer in Washington later Wednesday.
The uncertainty around trade has rattled investors, helping to overshadow U.S. economic data that has been healthy, including the Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing survey, which on Monday rose to 61.3 in August, its highest level since May 2004. The issue has undercut some confidence in the markets following a series of equity market records in recent weeks.
On top of that, investors are keeping a close eye on a steady unraveling of emerging economies as the U.S. dollar, perceived as a source of safety (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-draws-haven-flows-as-emerging-markets-face-renewed-pain-2018-09-04) for fretful investors, has strengthening amid the protracted trade spats. At the forefront of those worries are declines in the Turkish lira , Argentina's peso and the South African rand . The Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF (VWO) fell 1.5%.
What data and Fed speakers are ahead
The trade deficit soared almost 10% in July, hitting the highest level in five months (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-trade-deficit-soars-nearly-10-on-record-imports-2018-09-05) and keeping the U.S. on pace to record the largest annual gap in a decade.
Separately, a trio of Federal Reserve speakers are on deck. St. Louis President James Bullard speaks in the morning to discuss the economy and monetary policy at a conference in New York. On Tuesday, Bullard gave an interview with the Fox Business Network where he said the Fed should hold off on raising rates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bullard-says-fed-should-hold-off-on-raising-rates-2018-09-04).
Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari is slated to speak at 4 p.m. at a town hall forum in Bozeman, Mont., while Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic is scheduled to speak at a fireside chat at the Chicago Council on Global Affairs at 6:30 p.m.
What are market participants saying?
"We still see further upside in stocks, but we've had a nice run and it isn't uncommon to see a drawdown ahead of the midterm elections. Emerging-market contagion is a risk that's spilling into global equities, and while we still have a favorable view on the U.S., you need to be selective," said Matt Miskin, market strategist at John Hancock Financial Services.
What stocks are in focus?
Workday Inc. (WDAY) late Tuesday reported earnings that missed expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/workday-stock-declines-as-earnings-miss-drags-on-raised-outlook-2018-09-04) and raised its subscription outlook. Shares of the software company fell 9.5%.
RH(RH), the retailer formerly known as Restoration hardware, late Tuesday reported mixed second-quarter results, though it also raised its full-year profit outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/rh-formerly-restoration-hardware-ups-guidance-reports-mixed-quarter-2018-09-04). Shares fell 11%.
Vera Bradley Inc. (VRA) reported second-quarter earnings and revenue that beat expectations, sending shares up 15%.
HD Supply Holdings Inc.'s stock (HDS) fell 2.8% after the industrial distributor reported second-quarter results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hd-supply-earnings-revenue-beat-expectations-2018-09-05).
Sangamo Therapeutics Inc.'s stock (SGMO) fell 22% after the company released the results of a drug trial (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sangamo-stock-drops-13-premarket-on-results-of-phase-12-gene-editing-trial-2018-09-05).
What did other markets do?
Chinese stocks traded lower after a weeklong losing streak ended Tuesday. The Shanghai Composite traded down 1.7% and the Shenzhen Composite fell by 1.6%.
Meanwhile, Japan's Nikkei finished down 0.5%.
The U.S. dollar as measured by the ICE U.S. Dollar Index , a measure of the buck against six rivals, edged up 0.1% at 95.51 and have gained 0.4%, so far this week.
(END) 05, 2018 11:00 ET (15:00
